In [[number theory]], the '''''n'' conjecture''' is a [[conjecture]] stated by {{Harvtxt|Browkin|Brzeziński|1994}} as a generalization of the [[abc conjecture|''abc'' conjecture]] to more than three [[integer]]s.

== Formulations ==

Given <math>n \ge 3</math>, let <math>a_1,a_2,...,a_n \in \mathbb{Z}</math> satisfy three conditions:
: (i) <math>\gcd(a_1,a_2,...,a_n)=1</math>
: (ii) <math>a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_n = 0</math>
: (iii) no proper subsum of <math>a_1,a_2,...,a_n</math> equals <math>0</math>

'''First formulation'''

The ''n'' conjecture states that for every <math>\varepsilon>0</math>, there is a constant <math>C</math> depending on <math>n</math> and <math>\varepsilon</math>, such that:
<blockquote> <math>\operatorname{max}(|a_1|,|a_2|,...,|a_n|)< C_{n,\varepsilon}\operatorname{rad}(|a_1| \cdot |a_2| \cdot \ldots \cdot |a_n|)^{2n - 5 + \varepsilon}</math> </blockquote>
where <math>\operatorname{rad}(m)</math> denotes the [[radical of an integer|radical]] of an integer <math>m</math>, defined as the product of the distinct [[prime factor]]s of <math>m</math>.

'''Second formulation'''

Define the ''quality'' of <math>a_1,a_2,...,a_n</math> as
: <math>q(a_1,a_2,...,a_n) = \frac{\log(\operatorname{max}(|a_1|,|a_2|,...,|a_n|))}{\log(\operatorname{rad}(|a_1| \cdot |a_2| \cdot ... \cdot |a_n|))}</math>
The ''n'' conjecture states that <math>\limsup q(a_1,a_2,...,a_n)= 2n-5 </math>.

== Stronger form ==
{{Harvtxt|Vojta|1998}} proposed a stronger variant of the ''n'' conjecture, where setwise [[coprime]]ness of <math>a_1,a_2,...,a_n</math> is replaced by pairwise coprimeness of <math>a_1,a_2,...,a_n</math>.

There are two different formulations of this '''''strong n'' conjecture'''.

Given <math>n \ge 3</math>, let <math>a_1,a_2,...,a_n \in \mathbb{Z}</math> satisfy three conditions:
: (i) <math>a_1,a_2,...,a_n</math> are pairwise coprime
: (ii) <math>a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_n = 0</math>
: (iii) no proper subsum of <math>a_1,a_2,...,a_n</math> equals <math>0</math>

'''First formulation'''

The ''strong n'' conjecture states that for every <math>\varepsilon>0</math>, there is a constant <math>C</math> depending on <math>n</math> and <math>\varepsilon</math>, such that:
<blockquote> <math>\operatorname{max}(|a_1|,|a_2|,...,|a_n|)< C_{n,\varepsilon}\operatorname{rad}(|a_1| \cdot |a_2| \cdot \ldots \cdot |a_n|)^{1 + \varepsilon}</math> </blockquote>

'''Second formulation'''

Define the ''quality'' of <math>a_1,a_2,...,a_n</math> as
: <math>q(a_1,a_2,...,a_n) = \frac{\log(\operatorname{max}(|a_1|,|a_2|,...,|a_n|))}{\log(\operatorname{rad}(|a_1| \cdot |a_2| \cdot ... \cdot |a_n|))}</math>
The ''strong n'' conjecture states that <math>\limsup q(a_1,a_2,...,a_n) = 1</math>.

{{Harvtxt| Hölzl, Kleine and Stephan | 2025}} have shown that for <math>n \geq 5</math> the above limit superior is for odd <math>n</math> at least <math>5/3</math> and for even <math>n</math> is at least <math>5/4</math>. For the cases <math>n=3</math> (abc-conjecture) and <math>n=4</math>, they did not find any nontrivial lower bounds. It is also open whether there is a common constant upper bound above the limit superiors for all <math>n \geq 3</math>. For the exact status of the case <math>n=3</math> see the article on the [[abc conjecture]].
